title: A Midsummer Night's Tree: Efficient and High Performance Secure SCM
problem: Metadata for integrity verification (Bonsai Merkle Trees) cached in volatile on-chip caches may be lost during power failures in SCM systems. State-of-the-art lazy update crash-consistent metadata schemes optimize runtime overhead but neglect on-chip area efficiency.
motivation: Secure memory is critical to prevent memory corruption attacks, and the emergence of nonvolatile storage class memory (SCM) requires efficient crash-consistent metadata management to maintain integrity guarantees.
method: AMNT uses a nested 'tree within a tree' structure — organizing one tree hierarchy inside another — to keep integrity metadata safe even through sudden power failures. To save on-chip space, the design shifts bookkeeping work from hardware (the silicon chip) to software (the running program). Updates to this metadata are fine-tuned to remain fast while making good use of limited on-chip cache space.
key_novelty: A nested 'tree within a tree' structure that preserves file integrity tracking through power failures while saving on-chip area by shifting work from hardware to software.
contributions: Novel nested tree structure ('tree within a tree') for crash-consistent secure metadata in SCM
41% reduction in execution overhead compared to state-of-the-art lazy update schemes
Significant reduction in required on-chip area for security metadata
Software-based complexity offloading strategy to minimize hardware overhead
